summary:
Verified Kasubid Position Management feature set end-to-end. Backend: added /app/backend/tests/test_kasubid_feature.py with 16 tests covering kasubid info/status, set+replace (historical preservation), vacate, duplicate-same-person rejection, recap category filter (Semua/Staff/Kasubid with kasubid-ordered-first), exports (excel/pdf) with category param, and RBAC (operator/staff cannot set, operator can read roster). 16/16 PASS. Full backend suite: 58 collected, 53 pass + 1 skip + 4 known idempotency failures (same as iteration_2: TestTeamsEmployees.test_list_employees count drift from leftover TEST_ users, TestRollingIntegrity overlap, TestCommander already-set, TestReplacement conflict with prior start_date — all test-data artifacts, not product bugs). Frontend Playwright: Admin sees all three new nav items (Absensi Staff / Absensi Kasubid / Pengaturan Kasubid); Operator sees Absensi Staff + Absensi Kasubid but NOT Pengaturan Kasubid; Viewer sees neither; Staff sees only Dashboard + Absensi Saya — enumerated via document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid^="nav-"]'). Pengaturan Kasubid page shows pk-card-KASUBID1 and pk-card-KASUBID2, pk-set/pk-vacate/pk-hist buttons present and dialog opens. Absensi Kasubid: ks-input-date works, ks-roster-{id} lists active holders (2 on 2026-06-10 before test modifications). Rekap Bulanan rekap-category, Rekap Periode period-category, and Laporan Export lap-category selectors all visible and functional. Dashboard shows KASUBID 1 + KASUBID 2 cards with Status Aktif/Kosong.

BUG FOUND & FIXED: GET /api/recap/monthly?month=2026-09 and /api/recap/period?start=2026-01&end=2026-10 were returning HTTP 500 with 'TypeError: < not supported between instances of str and NoneType' in server.py line 681 (and sibling 666). Root cause: _compute_recap's breakdown and regu-ordering sort keys used tid (team_id) directly, but resolve_team_at() returns None for an employee whose attendance exists on a date for which no team assignment exists (possible after reassignment history edits). Fix: coalesce None to empty string in both sort keys. Verified: 2026-09 and the full period now return 200. Fix was pure defensive-coding (not business logic).

minor.issue: Resolver tie-breaking when a new assignment has the same start_date as a prior (now closed) assignment is implementation-defined — our second-run test picks a different winner. Consider ordering by created_at DESC on ties, or forbidding duplicate (position_id,start_date).

Body model KasubidIn requires employee_id but endpoint ignores it (uses body.position_id + body.start_date only). Accept a dedicated VacateIn model with just position_id + start_date, or make employee_id Optional, to avoid confusing callers.

action_items: (Optional) Review tie-break ordering in resolve_kasubid_for_date / resolve_team_at when multiple assignments share identical start_date; current result is undeterministic across sessions.
(Optional) Introduce VacateIn Pydantic model (position_id + start_date) and point POST /api/kasubid/vacate at it, instead of reusing KasubidIn with ignored employee_id.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 1713 lines — split into routers (kasubid.py, recap.py, export.py) is overdue.

_compute_recap: tid=None is a possible path (fixed sort), but downstream `teams.get(tid, {}).get('name', '-')` already handles None by returning '-'. Consider logging a warning when attendance exists without a team assignment on that date so admins notice stale data.
KasubidIn is reused for /kasubid, /kasubid/vacate, /commanders (via CommanderIn), /assignments — each ignores different fields; distinct DTOs would avoid confusion.
resolve_kasubid_for_date is called O(days * 2 positions) in _compute_kasubid_recap — preloading sub_unit_assignments once (like build_intervals for teams) would speed up long periods.

success_rate.backend: 100% on new feature (16/16); 53/58 on full suite (4 known-idempotency, same as iter2)
success_rate.frontend: 100% on new feature flows (nav labels, RBAC, pages render, testids present, no 500 modal after fix)

test_credentials: same as test_credentials.md: admin fransel.manuhutu@gmail.com / operator@damkar.go.id / kepala@damkar.go.id / staff@damkar.go.id / kasubid@damkar.go.id — all Damkar2026!
seed_data_creation: Replacement test created up to 2 new sub_unit_assignments for KASUBID2 (effective 2026-04-02 and 2026-07-02) + 1 attendance HDR on 2026-04-10 for emp_a. Vacate test closed K2 effective 2026-11-01. These persist. If the admin dashboard today shows K1=Kosong, it is a side-effect of a prior test iteration (not this one); production data was never modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The recap endpoints are now resilient to None team_id in breakdown rows (fixed in iteration_3). Nav testid pattern: nav-{path-no-leading-slash}, e.g. nav-input-absensi (for /input-absensi path which displays label 'Absensi Staff'), nav-absensi-kasubid, nav-pengaturan-kasubid. For dashboard, kasubid cards use literal 'KASUBID 1' / 'KASUBID 2' (uppercase, with space). AbsensiKasubid route is /absensi-kasubid; empty-state element data-testid='ks-empty' shows when no active kasubid on selected date; otherwise rows ks-roster-{employee_id} and batch buttons ks-batch-{HDR|OFF|SKT|TK|IZN|DL}-btn. On re-runs, 4 pre-existing backend tests will fail due to state mutation (list_employees count, rolling overlap, commander already-set, replacement start_date collision) — these are flaky-on-rerun by design and were already noted in iteration_2.
rca of the issue: 500 on /api/recap/monthly for 2026-09 and /api/recap/period 2026-01..2026-10: _compute_recap built breakdown map keyed by (eid, tid, month) where tid came from resolve_team_at (returns None for an employee whose attendance exists without a corresponding team assignment on that day). Python 3 cannot compare None to str inside the sort key `lambda kv: (kv[0][2], kv[0][1])`. Reproduction: GET /api/recap/period?start=2026-01&end=2026-10 as admin. Mitigation: coalesce None to '' in sort keys at server.py lines 666 and 681. Verified fixed. Also recommend investigating WHY an attendance record has no concurrent team assignment — likely a historical team reassignment left a gap, which the test suite's rolling test can produce.
